Novelty Can Mustache Clip vs Hiccup Mustache Straws

Two ridiculous drink accessories. One wins for laughs, the other for practicality. Let's settle this.

Every dad, uncle, or party host has seen them: those clip-on plastic mustaches that turn an ordinary soda can into a handlebar masterpiece. Then there's the other camp — silicone mustache-shaped straw toppers that slip over your drink tab and keep things clean. Both promise laughs. Only one earns its spot in the junk drawer (or the next white elephant gift exchange).

Cost, staying power, washability, and raw comedic value — here's the real breakdown.

Novelty Can Mustache Clip — Pros

  • Instant laugh — the visual gag works every single time
  • Hard plastic construction won't tear or deform after repeated clip-ons
  • Universally fits 12oz standard cans (beer, soda, seltzer)
  • Perfect white elephant, secret santa, or gag gift price point
  • Sits above the can opening — doesn't interfere with drinking
  • Instagrammable — guaranteed to end up in someone's story

Novelty Can Mustache Clip — Cons

  • Single-use joke territory — once the novelty wears off, it collects dust
  • Hard plastic — not dishwasher-safe; stubborn grime in crevices
  • Only fits 12oz cans — won't work on skinny cans, glass bottles, or tallboys
  • $17.99 for a single clip is steep compared to multi-pack alternatives
  • Doesn't provide any hygiene function — purely decorative
  • Can snap off if dropped or bumped — not great for tailgates

Hiccup Mustache Straws — Pros

  • Dishwasher-safe silicone — easy to sanitize between uses
  • 4-pack means you can share with friends or rotate styles
  • Creates a hygienic barrier over the can tab — great for garage, workshop, or dusty festivals
  • Built-in straw makes drinking smoother and cleaner
  • Fits more can sizes including tallboys
  • At $9.99 for 4, way more value per unit

Hiccup Mustache Straws — Cons

  • Subtler visual — doesn't land the same instant laugh as a full clip-on mustache
  • Silicone can pick up lint and dust if stored loose in a drawer
  • The straw is short — you're still sipping near the can rim
  • Mustache designs are less defined — from a distance it just looks like a colored tab cover
  • Softer gag factor — more practical, less comedic

Our Pick: Novelty Can Mustache Clip

Hear us out: this isn't about which product is more useful — it's about which one delivers what it promises. The Novelty Can Mustache Clip promises laughs and it delivers them at 100% volume. It's the item people pass around, photograph, and talk about all night. For Father's Day, gag gifts, and party moments, nothing beats it.

The Hiccup Mustache Straws are the smarter, cheaper, more practical product — but they live in a weird middle ground where they're not funny enough to be a gag gift and not practical enough to replace a regular drink cover. For sheer comedy value and giftability, the clip-on mustache takes the crown.
